Building and Running

examples/general/thread_pool.cpp, one source file built by examples/CMakeLists.txt as thread_pool (cmake-build/examples/thread_pool on Linux, cmake-build\examples\Release\thread_pool.exe on Windows) and run by tests/run_tests.sh. See Building and Running for the build commands. The comment at the top of the file describes the program. Back to the example programs.

ThreadPool demo. Submits tasks that return values and one that
throws, then collects the results from the futures.

Usage: thread_pool [threads]
*/
// ----------------------------------------------------------- // 
#include "gxdlcode.h"

#include <cstdlib>
#include <iostream>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <vector>
#include "thrpool.h"

using namespace datareel;

static long long sum_to(long long n)
{
  long long s = 0;
  for(long long i = 1; i <= n; i++) s += i;
  return s;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
  std::size_t threads = argc > 1 ? (std::size_t)std::atoi(argv[1]) : 0;
  ThreadPool pool(threads);
  std::cout << "Pool has " << pool.Size() << " threads\n";

  std::vector<std::future<long long>> results;
  for(long long n = 1000; n <= 5000; n += 1000) {
    results.push_back(pool.Submit(sum_to, n));
  }
  auto bad = pool.Submit([]() -> int { throw std::runtime_error("task failed"); });

  int errors = 0;
  long long n = 1000;
  for(auto &r : results) {
    long long v = r.get();
    std::cout << "sum_to(" << n << ") = " << v << "\n";
    if(v != n * (n + 1) / 2) errors++;
    n += 1000;
  }
  try {
    bad.get();
    errors++;
  }
  catch(const std::exception &e) {
    std::cout << "Exception from task: " << e.what() << "\n";
  }
  pool.Wait();
  return errors == 0 ? 0 : 1;
}
